newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Wage deal to cost Venezuela added $314 mln - source.
newsitem.headline: Wage deal to cost Venezuela added $314 mln - source.

text.p: A new deal reached by the Venezuelan government late Tuesday over public sector pay rises will add 150 billion bolivars ($314 million) to the amount budgeted for pay increases, a well-placed source at the Planning Ministry told Reuters.
"That's equivalent to an increase of some 0.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP)," said the source, who asked not to be identified.

Budgeted public sector wage increases had previously been set at 1.25 trillion bolivars ($2.6 billion), the source said. That figure included an average 35 percent across-the-board pay rise offered to Venezuela's 1.2 million public sector workers in early February.
That offer would have shaved Venezuela's projected budget surplus to some 0.8 percent of GDP from year-end forecasts of around 1.4 percent.
The pact finally reached last night would further cut that ratio.
Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar did not comment Tuesday on the new deal's possible impact on the budget or inflation.

With the economy rocked by strikes since workers rejected a 25 percent average increase in January, Matos said: "The agreement shows that if there is a will, it is possible in Venezuela ... to reach understandings which avoid conflict."
No figures were immediately available as to how much the new offer translated into an average percentage increase.
Matos said the agreed raise was higher than an official inflation estimate for the year -- currently between 25 and 35 percent.
According to local reports, blue collar workers will receive a 50 percent rise under the terms of the agreement, and white collar workers a 78 percent increase.
Venezuela has been rocked since January by a series of public sector strikes to protest real wages slashed by years of inflation to 30 percent of 1980 levels.
